IT IS BEST TO USE A LARGE, LEVEL GROUND AREA FOR STORAGE. MAKE SURE THE FIREWOOD IS STACKED IN A HORIZONTAL WAY TO PREVENT DAMAGE. USE A PILE OF AT LEAST FOUR STACKS FOR STABILITY. EACH STACK SHOULD BE AT LEAST FIVE FEET HIGH. CHECK THE FIREWOOD EVERY TWO WEEKS TO MAKE SURE IT IS NOT ROTTING. USE A BAG OR A TIRE TO COVER THE FIREWOOD TO PREVENT WEATHER DAMAGE. KEEP A DISTANCE OF AT LEAST TWO FEET BETWEEN STACKS TO ALLOW FOR AIRFLOW. DO NOT STORE FIREWOOD NEAR POWER LINES OR ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT. MAKE SURE TO REMOVE ANY ROTTEN OR DAMAGED LOGS AS THEY GROW. THIS WILL HELP KEEP THE FIREWOOD CLEAN AND SAFE FOR THE WINTER. ALL NEIGHBORS SHOULD BE INFORMED OF THE FIREWOOD STORAGE LOCATION TO FACILITATE ACCESS. THE FIREWOOD SHOULD BE STORED IN A PLACE THAT IS EASY TO REACH AND SAFE TO HANDLE.  

**IN SUMMARY:** STORING FIREWOOD PROPERLY IS A NECESSARY STEP FOR A SAFE AND COMFORTABLE WINTER. FOLLOW THESE SIMPLE GUIDELINES TO HELP KEEP YOUR NEIGH
